newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK airport authority reacts to IATA criticism.
newsitem.headline: HK airport authority reacts to IATA criticism.

text.p: HONG KONG, Feb 27 (Reuter) A spokesman for the Hong Kong Airport Authority said the Chek Lap Kok fee structure has not yet been decided and will not be until after airlines are consulted at the fifth round of talks next month.

On Tuesday the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said Hong Kong could lose a million passengers a year if moves to introduce high airline charges at its new Chek Lap Kok airport went ahead.

The Airport Authority official discounted reports that fees would quadruple as "entire speculation" and said "we are looking at running a good business in partnership with the airlines and we will not make any money if the airlines don't come to Hong Kong."
He said the state of the art facilities at Chek Lap Kok are incomparable with present facilities at Kai Tak.

"As to the charge that we are not aware of the contribution that Chek Lap Kok will have to Hong Kong's economy, of course we are and nothing demonstrates that more than the huge investment in providing the new airport. We are fully conscious of the economic benefits," he added.

He said the market value of Chek Lap Kok will not be factored into new landing fees and that the issues raised by IATA of using the prime land fees from the redevelopment of Kai Tak to offset landing charges and the question of reviewing the intended five per cent real rate of return on the new airport investment were matters of government policy and not for the Authority.

The real rate of return of five per cent was a "prudent commercial return" which had been set by the Hong Kong Government and was outside the Authority's control, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
